faqs.question: What is the California income tax rate?
faqs.answer: California has progressive tax rates up to 13.3%.

faqs.question: Does California tax Social Security?
faqs.answer: California does not tax Social Security benefits at the state level.

faqs.question: How do I file California state taxes?
faqs.answer: You can file California state taxes online through the state's Department of Revenue website, or use tax preparation software.

faqs.question: What deductions are available in California?
faqs.answer: California offers standard deductions and may allow itemized deductions. Check the state tax authority for current amounts.

faqs.question: When are California state taxes due?
faqs.answer: California state income taxes are typically due April 15, the same date as federal taxes, unless an extension is filed.

faqs.answer: Property tax is calculated by multiplying your home's assessed value by the local tax rate. Rates vary by county and municipality.

faqs.question: Are there property tax exemptions in California?

faqs.question: Does California tax capital gains?
faqs.answer: Yes, California taxes capital gains at rates up to 13.3%.

faqs.question: Are long-term and short-term gains taxed differently in California?
faqs.answer: At the state level, most states tax both types as ordinary income. The federal government offers lower rates for long-term gains.

faqs.question: How can I reduce capital gains tax in California?
faqs.answer: Strategies include holding investments for over a year, tax-loss harvesting, using retirement accounts, and utilizing the primary residence exclusion.

faqs.question: Is there a capital gains exemption in California?
faqs.answer: California follows federal exemptions for primary residence sales ($250K single, $500K married) and may offer additional deductions.

faqs.question: When do I owe California capital gains tax?
faqs.answer: Capital gains tax is due when you file your annual state tax return, typically by April 15.

faqs.question: Does California have an inheritance tax?
faqs.answer: Check with the state's Department of Revenue for current inheritance tax laws, as they differ from estate taxes.

faqs.question: How can I reduce estate taxes in California?

faqs.question: Is the federal estate tax different from California's?
faqs.answer: Yes, the federal estate tax is separate with its own exemption ($13.61M in 2024). You may owe both if applicable.

faqs.question: What is the effective tax rate in California?
faqs.answer: It depends on your income level. California state taxes are up to 13.3%, plus federal taxes and FICA.

faqs.question: How is effective tax rate different from marginal rate?
faqs.answer: Marginal rate is the tax on your last dollar of income. Effective rate is your total tax divided by total income — typically lower.

faqs.question: What taxes are included in the effective rate?
faqs.answer: Federal income tax, state income tax, Social Security tax (6.2%), and Medicare tax (1.45%).

faqs.question: How can I lower my effective tax rate?
faqs.answer: Maximize pre-tax deductions (401k, HSA), itemize deductions, use tax credits, and consider tax-loss harvesting.

faqs.question: Does California have local income taxes too?
faqs.answer: Some California localities may impose additional income taxes. Check with your city or county.

calculators.name: California Self-Employment Tax Calculator
calculators.metaDescription: Calculate self-employment tax in California. See SE tax, state income tax, and quarterly payment estimates.
calculators.heroSubtitle: Estimate your total self-employment tax burden in California
calculators.introText: Self-employed workers in California pay 15.3% in SE tax (Social Security 12.4% + Medicare 2.9%) on 92.35% of net earnings, plus state income tax up to 13.3%.
calculators.formula: SE Tax = Net Earnings × 92.35% × 15.3% (SS capped at $168,600)

faqs.question: How much is self-employment tax in California?
faqs.answer: The federal SE tax rate is 15.3% on 92.35% of net earnings. Plus California state income tax.

faqs.question: Do I need to pay quarterly taxes in California?
faqs.answer: Yes, self-employed individuals must make estimated quarterly payments if they expect to owe $1,000+ in taxes.

faqs.question: Can I deduct half of SE tax?
faqs.answer: Yes, you can deduct 50% of your self-employment tax when calculating your adjusted gross income.

faqs.question: What expenses can I deduct in California?
faqs.answer: Common deductions include home office, vehicle, health insurance, supplies, and professional services.

faqs.question: When are quarterly payments due?
faqs.answer: Quarterly estimated tax payments are due April 15, June 15, September 15, and January 15.
